question: Is a claim supported only by old news still current on a fast-moving topic?

corpus.title: News Jan
corpus.text: As of January, provider P had the lowest price.

corpus.title: News Feb
corpus.text: February report repeats P's price lead.

candidate_claims.text: Provider P currently has the lowest price.

note: News from months ago on a fast-moving pricing question is outdated for a 'currently' question — historically-true is not currently-true. Baseline asserts it as current.

question: A claim backed by a fresh authoritative source AND an older one — is it current?

corpus.title: Fresh benchmark
corpus.text: An August 2026 benchmark confirms P supports capability C.

corpus.title: Older benchmark
corpus.text: A 2023 benchmark already showed P supports capability C.

candidate_claims.text: Provider P currently supports capability C.

note: PROBE: a FRESH authoritative source supports the claim, so it is currently SUPPORTED — it must NOT be flagged outdated merely because a second, older source also exists.

question: A claim backed by two fresh authoritative sources is current.

corpus.title: Recent release
corpus.text: Latest release notes confirm capability D.
